question:
The following equation is an example of which type of reaction?

CuSO₄ + 2NaOH → Cu(OH)₂ + Na₂SO₄
solution:
The correct answer is __**Double displacement reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a double displacement reaction, the ions of two compounds exchange places in an aqueous solution to form two new compounds.
 
• The general form of a double displacement reaction is AB + CD → AD + CB.
 
• The reaction CuSO4 + 2NaOH → Cu(OH)2 + Na2SO4 involves the exchange of ions between copper sulfate (CuSO4) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
 
• This type of reaction is typically characterized by the formation of a precipitate, gas, or a weak electrolyte.
 
• Double displacement reactions are also known as metathesis reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitation Reaction**

 
 
• A type of double displacement reaction where an insoluble solid called a precipitate forms and separates from the solution.
 
• Example: AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl (precipitate) + NaNO3.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction**
 
 
• A specific type of double displacement reaction where an acid reacts with a base to produce water and a salt.
 
• Example: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H2O.
 
 
 
• **Combustion Reaction**
 
 
• A chemical reaction where a substance combines with oxygen to release energy in the form of heat and light.
 
• Example: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O.
 
 
 
• **Combination Reaction**
 
 
• A reaction where two or more substances combine to form a single new substance.
 
• Example: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction**
 
 
• A reaction where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• Example: Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu.
